cfg.title: Configuration
cfg.opt.rules: rules (game rule commander, no LLM calls)
cfg.engineHelp: Main switch. rules: the sidecar answers with no orders so the game's own rule commander drives; the HQ scheduler is idle. model: a future trained decision model.
cfg.keyStored: stored key ending ...{0} (leave empty to keep)
cfg.keyNote: Write-only: the sidecar never sends the key back.
cfg.minInterval: Min interval per faction (s, 0 = every request)
cfg.batchNote: Batch APIs (24 h latency) don't fit a live war, so we cut call frequency instead. Skipped requests answer "keep current orders". The min interval is the hard floor between any two LLM calls (also for wakeups and triggers); unchanged situations are skipped at scheduled wakeups.
cfg.w.dynamic: Let the LLM choose its next wakeup (next_check_sec)
cfg.w.stretch: Stretch intervals when the budget pace overshoots
cfg.wakeNote: The game polls every 10 s; the HQ is only consulted at the scheduled time or when a trigger fires. With dynamic off the interval is always the default. Budget stretch multiplies the interval by projected/limit (max x3) when the OpenRouter pace estimate projects overshooting the key limit.
cfg.tr.enabled: Wake the HQ early on events
cfg.tr.newContact: New contact (more than 150 m from every known one)
cfg.tr.objectiveReached: Objective reached (within 50 m, or squad idle)
cfg.tr.strengthDrop: Squad strength drop (% of start, 0 = off)
cfg.tr.ticketsDrop: Own tickets dropped since last call (%, 0 = off, v2)
cfg.trNote: Compared with the situation at the last LLM call. Triggered calls also respect the min interval above. Use "wake now" in the status strip to force a call.
cfg.stopAtLimit: Stop provider calls at the key's spending limit
cfg.stopAtLimitNote: (the game then runs on its rule commander; LLM resumes automatically when budget is available again)
cfg.enabledNote: (off: no LLM calls, the game runs on its rule commander; the HQ engine selector above is the main switch)
cfg.testing: testing with the form values (nothing is saved)...
use.title: Usage
use.stopped: Provider calls are stopped; the game uses its rule commander until budget is available again.
use.pctUsed: {0}% of the key's spending limit used ({1} left).
use.overshoot: At this pace you will overshoot by {0} by reset.
use.noKey: No API key stored: budget polling is off.
use.lastPoll: last poll {0}; session figures reset when the sidecar restarts
use.keyAdvice: Use a dedicated OpenRouter key with a hard spending limit.
cfg.strongNote: Commander, HQ replies and the war journal. Used for every call except translation (when a weak LLM is set).
cfg.weakNote: A cheap model for translating broadcast text (SITREP, announcements). None: the strong LLM translates.
cfg.i18nEnabledNote: SITREPs and announcements are also written in each recipient's language. Off: English only.
fb.title: Backup model (used when the main model is rate-limited or fails)
fb.note: On HTTP 429, 5xx, a timeout or a network error the call is retried once on the backup model. Errors such as 400/401 do not switch. Leave the model empty for no backup.
fb.modelPh: e.g. a paid model on the same provider
fb.inherit: Empty = same as the main model.
fb.keyNote: Write-only. Empty = the main key, reused only while provider and URL stay the same.
fb.tip: The main model failed ({0}); the backup model answered.
fb.chipTip: Calls answered by a backup model: strong {0}, weak {1}
fb.coolTip: These models were rate-limited or failed recently and are skipped for a short while; the backup model is used meanwhile.

cfg.l.title: LLM latency
cfg.l.note: Settings that trade prompt size, call count and model strength against reply time. See the Latency tab for the effect.
cfg.l.reasoningHelp: Hidden thinking before the answer, for every call incl. /hq. On reasoning models it takes most of the time (ling-3.1-flash: 9 s instead of 1.5 s).
cfg.l.modeHelp: How the provider is asked for JSON. If a model rejects the format, the call is retried once without it.
cfg.l.terseHelp: The model answers with short arrays instead of verbose objects: fewer output tokens, faster replies.
cfg.l.plannerHelp: On: purchases and FOB logistics come from a slower background call, the orders call stays small. Off: they stay in the orders call.
cfg.l.rolesHelp: Which slot answers each role. A role on the weak slot uses the strong one while no weak slot is configured.
cfg.l.escalateHelp: Commander calls woken by an important trigger (contact near a squad, casualties, squad lost, objective change, tickets drop) use this slot; routine ticks use the commander role above.
cfg.l.timeoutsHelp: 0 = use the timeout of the slot. A slow role then no longer cools down the others.
cfg.l.promptHelp: Lean: compact tables, only relevant contacts. Static block: rarely changing facts go first so the provider can cache the prompt prefix.
cfg.l.sitrepHelp: The SITREP is its own background call on the slot of the sitrep role (see Model per role) and is delivered with the next poll reply. It no longer slows down the orders call.
